title: Autonomous Synthetic Workload Composer & CI Gatekeeper for Token/sec Regressions
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Build an autonomous synthetic workload composer and CI gatekeeper that creates small, statistically-efficient microbenchmarks for PRs and decides pass/fail for performance regressions (tokens/sec, p95). This ticket covers workload synthesis, baseline curation, analysis engine, CI integration, and observability.
acceptance_criteria:
1) CI runs generate a deterministic synthetic micro-workload per PR that approximates target production token distribution.
2) The baseline curator picks the appropriate historical baseline slice automatically.
3) The analysis engine computes a probabilistic regression score (posterior probability of >=5% drop in tokens/sec.p95) and outputs pass/fail/soft-fail.
4) PR comments and status checks are emitted; soft-fails annotate the PR but do not block for the first two occurrences.
5) Metrics are stored in Grafana with 90-day retention; dashboards show baseline drift and confidence intervals.
design_notes:
- Workload composer: sample from recent request histogram (sequence-length, prompt-type, tokenization buckets) and synthesize ~50 short sessions that exercise KV cache and typical prefix reuse.
- Warmup: include a brief warmup phase to prime KV cache (configurable).
- Baseline curation: use sliding-window percentile-matching; prefer last N successful merges from main, exclude suspect releases.
- Analysis: Bayesian sequential test (Beta/Normal conjugate approximations) to compute posterior probability of >5% drop in tokens/sec.p95. Use hierarchical noise model to borrow strength across similar PRs.
- Gate policy: posterior >= 0.95 -> hard-fail; 0.80-0.95 -> soft-fail (annotate and require manual triage); <0.80 -> pass.
- CI integration: GitHub Actions step uploads raw samples, analysis runs in a small container, result posted as check-run with link to dashboard.
- Rollout: start with non-blocking rollout to internal teams, then opt-in for blocking for release branches.
implementation_plan: 1) Implement workload composer library (Go) + sampling config. 2) Baseline curator service + small DB table for curated slices. 3) Analysis engine (Python) with unit tests and statistical simulation harness. 4) CI action + GitHub status reporter. 5) Grafana dashboards and alerts. 6) Internal dogfood for 2 weeks, collect signal, tune thresholds. 7) Promote to blocking for release branches.
tasks: Implement composer: sequence-length and prefix reuse sampling
Implement Bayesian analysis and unit tests
Add GitHub Action and status check
Run 2-week internal rollout and collect results
Write runbook for triage and false-positive handling
test_plan:
- Unit tests for composer sampling correctness.
- Synthetic A/B tests: simulate 0%, 3%, 6%, 10% regressions, verify posterior calibration and gating decision rates.
- Staging CI runs on known-good commits to measure false-positive rate target <3%.
- Canary: enable non-blocking for 10 active PRs from infra teams for 2 weeks and collect posteriors and manual triage outcomes.
risks_and_mitigations:
Risk: noisy microbenchmarks produce false positives. Mitigation: hierarchical noise model and soft-fail policy; require repeat detection for hard-fail promotion.
Risk: synthetic workload diverges from production. Mitigation: periodic re-calibration against sampled production traces and telemetry.
Risk: CI runtime cost. Mitigation: small sample size, caching, and off-peak scheduling for heavy runs.
